Indian Standard 



DETERMINATION OF TOTAL CARBON 
IN HARDMETALS BY GRAVIMETRIC METHOD 



3 



5 
o 
Q_ 



1. Scope 

1.1 This standard specifies a gravimetric method for determination of the total carbon content in 
carbides ar\6 hardmetals. 

1.2 This method is applicable to the following having a total carbon content exceeding 4 percent: 

a) Carbides of chromium, hafnium, molybdenum, niobium, tantalum, titanium, vanadium, tungsten 
and zirconium; 

b) Mixture of these carbides and binder metals, free of lubricant; and 

c) All grades of presintered or sintered hardmetals produced from these carbides. 

2. Principle . 

2.1» Oxidation of carbon to carbon dioxide at high temperature in a stream of pure oxygen, with the 
addition of a flux, if necessary. Absorption of carbon dioxide carried by oxygen, by soda asbestos 
(ascarite) in a tared bulb. Determination of increase in mass of the soda 'asbestos (ascarite) which 
corresponds to the quantity of carbon dioxide formed. 



C + 0, ^ CO2 
2NaOH4-C02- 



Na.COs + HsO 



3. Reagents — During the analysis, use only reagents of analytical grade and distilled water or 
water of equivalent purity. 

* 

3.1 Ox/flre/7 — With a limitation of carbon containing impurities <0"6 ml of carbon per cubic metre 
of oxygen ( medical oxygen is preferred ). 

3.2 Magnesium Perch/orate [ Mg ( 0104)2. Mol Wt = 2232] — Anhydrous. 

Caution : To prevent any possibility of explosion, contact of this reagent witlt organic materials should 
be avoided, specially when discarding it. 

33 Flux— For example tin metal, copper metal or oxide, iron metal. 

ZA Soda Asbestos (Ascarite) —\n granules of about 2 mm diameter, impregnated with sodium 
hydro^cidlfe solution. As far as possible, avoid contact with air. 

4. Apparatus 

4.0 Ordinary Laboratory Apparatus 

4.1 Apparatus — Consisting of an electric furnace with a combustion tube, a purification train and 
system \6 absorb carbon dioxide. If necessary to obtain oxygen of adequate purity, an oxygen 
purification train may also be used. 

Successive parts of the apparatus shall be joined together with connecting tubes ( for example 
lattice tube ) forming an airtight seal. The apparatus is shown schematically in Fig. 1.

A — Source of oxygen (3.1 ), with pressure-regulating valve 

B — Flow meter 

C — Unit to dry and purify the oxygen (3.2). containing anhydrous n^agnesium perchiorate 
( 3.2 ) and soda asbestos ( ascarlte ) ( 3.4 ), separated with glass wool or silica wool. The 
diameter of the unit should be 25 mm and the length 100 mm approximately 

D — Electric furnance capable of operation at up to 1 SSCC, with a suitable device for tempera- 
ture control 

E — Combustion tube made of a non-porous refractory material. The internal diameter of the tube 
should be 18 to 24 mm and its length at least 650 to 700 mm 

F — Boat made of a refractory material, pretreated in an oxygen stream at the test temperature for 
10 min, or alternatively at 800 to 1 OOOX for 1 hour 

The boat shall be of suitable dimensions, for example length 80 to 100 mm, width 12 to 
14 mm and depth 7 to 9 mm 

The pretreated boats shall be kept in a desiccator. The ground surfaces of the desiccator and 
its lid shall not be greased 

G — Plug of silica wool or calcined asbestos wool 

H — Cooling system made of transparent glass with the internal diameter of the tube 5 to 7 mm 
and covered by flow of water, so that the temperature of gas does not reach higher than 60X 
during the operation 

/ —- Drying bulb containing anhydrous magnesium perchiorate ( 3.2 ) 

J — Absorption bulb containing soda asbestos ( ascarlte ) ( 3.4 ) and small amount of anhydrous 
magnesium perchiorate (3.2) 

A typical absorption bulb is shown in Fig. 2.

4.2 //ooit — Made from heat-resisting metal wire with a carbon content less than 005 percent. Its 
diameter should be approximately 3 mm and its length 500 to 600 mm. 

5. Sampling 

5.1 The sample shall be crushed to a powder in a mortar made of a material which does not alter the 
sample composition. The powder shall pass through 180 ftm sieve. 

Note — For sintered hardmetals, the preparation of sample shall be agreed to between the purchaser and the 
manufacturer. 

5.2 The analysis shall be carried out on two cr three test portions. 

6. Procedure 

6.1 Check the temperature in the combustion zone ( 1 200 to 1 350X, and not less than 1 300°C, if 
chromium carbide is present), the gas tightness of the apparatus and the efficiency of the oxygen 
purification. Pass oxygen through the apparatus for 10 to 15 min at a rate of 300 to 500 cm^min 
depending on the diameter of the tube used. Then disconnect the absorption bulbs (J), weigh 
them at ambient temperature and replace them in position. 



18:12539-1988 

6.2 Te^f Por^b/7 — The mass of the test portion { /77o ) shall be such that it contains approximately 
003 g of carbon, and shall be determined to the nearest 000 1 g. 

If necessary, add to the test portion 0'2 to 1 g of flux ( 3.3 ). 

6.3 Blank Test — Carry out the blank test by combustion ( proceed as outlined in 6.4 and 6.5 ) in the 
presence of the quantity of flux used in the analysis, and carefully determine the increase in mass ( mi ) 
of the absorption bulbs. 

6.4 Combust/on — Open the combustion tube at the oxygen inlet end and, using the hook ( 4.2 ), 
place the boat containing the test portion in the centre of the heated zone of the tube. Quickly close, 
the tube and immediately pass a stream of oxygen at a rate of 300 to 500 cm^min, depending on the 
diameter of the tube used. Continue to pass oxygen for 10 to 20 min so that the carbon dioxide is 
completely removed from the combustion tube and the purifying bulb. 

6.5 Determination — Close the taps of the absorption bulbs {J) and immediately remove the bulbs 
from the apparatus. When they are at ambient temperature, open and then rapidly close the taps to 
equalize the pressure and then weigh the bulbs to the nearest 0000 1 g. It Is recommended that the 
fused mass in the boat be visually examined to verify that combustion has been completed. The 
increase in mass represents the carbon dioxide absorbed ( mi ). 

7. Test Results 

7.1 Calculation — The carbon content expressed as a percentage by mass, is given by the formula. 

Total carbon, percent by mass ^ 27 29 x — ^—^ 

/77o 

where 

/77o = mass, in g, of the test portion; 

mi = mass, in g, of carbon dioxide obtained from the blank test; 

mz — mass, In g, of the carbon dioxide obtained from the combustion of the test portion; and 
27'29 = carbon dioxide to carbon conversion factor, multiplied by 100. 

7.2 Tolerance — The deviation between two or three independent determinations shall not exceed the 
values shown In Table 1.

7.3 Final Result — Report the arithmetical mean of acceptable determinations rounded to the nearest 
001 percent. 

8. Test Report — The test report shall include the following information: 

a) Reference to this standard, 

b) All details necessary for identification of the test sample, 

c) The result obtained, and 

d) Details of any occurrence which may have affected the result. 



EXPLANATORY NOTE 

In the preparation of this standard, assistance has been derived from ISO 3907-1 985 'Hardmetals — 
Determination of total carbon content — Gravimetric method', issued by the International Organization 
for Standardization ( ISO).
